case_name: G. Vivekanandan v Sriramulu and Others

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division bench of the Madras High Court directing acquittal of the accused persons who faced trial for alleged commission of offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC').

Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Virudhunagar had held the respondent accused persons guilty for causing the death of one Gurusamy Naicker (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') on 25.5.1997 while he was sleeping in front of a shop.
The deceased and one Veerasamy pacified the accused and others.
On 23.05.1997 at about 10.00 p.m., all the four accused went to the hotel of the deceased Guruswamy Naicker.
At about 3.45 a.m. on 25.05.1997 PWs.1and 2 for the purpose of opening the hotel, were making preparations by cleaning the hotel.

When the accused reached the deceased, A-3 caught hold of the legs of the deceased and A-4 uttered the words, 'cut and kill him', whereupon A-1 with MO I aruval in his hands cut on the left side of the neck of the deceased.
After the accused left, PWs. 1 to 4 went near the deceased and they saw the deceased had no life,
The body of the deceased was then sent to the Government Hospital with a requisition to conduct post mortem.
Dr. Bharathilakslmi (P.W.l1) at Goverment Hospital, Rajapalayam, on receipt of requisition Ex.P-13 commenced autopsy on the body of the deceased at about 3.00 PM in the afternoon.
petitioner_arguments: The evidence of PWs.1 & 2 has been discarded without indicating any reason.
It was also pointed out that there is no delay in dispatching to Magistrate (Ex.19).
No reason has been indicated as to why the detailed analysis done by the Trial Court deserved to be up set.
court_reasoning: The High Court has not discussed the evidence.
No reason has been indicated as to why the detailed analysis done by the Trial Court deserved to be up set.
holding: The appeal is remitted to the High Court for fresh disposal in accordance with law.
